items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: he wasn’t even leading the thing it was like he was a side person like myself but so it was like really a great combination of people: Gary Bartz, Christian McBride, Kenny Werner

ctx.x: Was that a situation that you were in when you played with him? Like no chordal instrument?

No this particular thing — he wasn’t even leading the thing it was like he was a side person like myself but so it was like really a great combination of people: Gary Bartz, Christian McBride, Kenny Werner, so it was kind of a cool thing. It was like three horns, rhythm section, and he was on it, this singer Roseanna Vitro, and it was like, so we started talking and so we’re both from the Detroit area, talking about — he’s older than me obviously but people that he knew and that I played with when I was growing…

“We’re going on the road soon, give her your number.” Because we need — because it was like between saxophone players. It was after Pat LaBarbera had stopped playing with him, who was a great musician from Upstate New York. And it was just like I wasn’t ready. In my mind I wasn’t — first of all I’d never be ready. He’s Elvin Jones. But man, I’m glad I got the experience and I would have loved to have played six nights a week.
